issues.description: The problem statement (text and UML) specifies a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the method signature (adds a parameter) compared to the specification and UML. Additionally, other solution methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents, getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) call getTotalNumberOfStudents(true), coupling their implementations to the boolean parameter. Students following the problem statement / UML will implement a no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents(), which will not match the solution's signature and may cause confusion or test mismatches.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the implementation with the problem specification and UML by changing the solution to provide a no-argument method: public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(). Implement it to return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. Then update other methods in the solution to call the no-arg method (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents() should call getTotalNumberOfStudents()). Alternatively, if the intended design truly requires an option to include/exclude guests, update the problem statement and UML to document getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (and provide both the boolean variant and a convenience no-arg overload) so the signature in the solution matches the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int (no parameters) that returns the total number of students. In the solution implementation the method is present but with a different signature: getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This parameterized form changes the API expected by the exercise (and how students will reason about 'total number of students'), forcing students to reconcile a different method contract between the specification and the reference implementation. This mismatch can lead to confusion about which method to implement, failing tests that expect the no-argument form, and extra cognitive load mapping the requirement to the solution.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the solution with the problem specification by providing a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total number of students (including guests, per the exercise intent). Options: (a) change the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() and return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; or (b) add an overload public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that delegates to the existing boolean variant (e.g., return getTotalNumberOfStudents(true)). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to explicitly document the boolean parameter if that was intentional. Prefer (a) or (b) so the API matches the UML and student expectations.
